senses.gloss:
1. Dhava is the name of a tree (Grislea tormentosa) mentioned, together with the plakṣa, aśvattha, and Khādira, in the Atharvaveda.
Foot notes v. 5, 5; xx. 137, 11. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 62.

2. Dhava, ‘man,’ is not found before the nirukta. The word clearly owes its existence merely to vidhavā, ‘widow,’ wrongly interpreted as vi-dhavā, ‘without a husband.’
Foot notes iii. 15. Cf. Naighaṇṭuka, ii. 3.

Dhavitra, occurring in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa and the taittirīya Āraṇyaka, denotes a ‘fan’ of hide or leather for blowing the sacrificial fire.
Foot notes xiv. 1, 3, 30; 3, 1, 21.
v. 4, 33.
